items.title: A message from the founder
items.body:
To everyone representing NOREX UNITED,

I appreciate everyone who has been part of NOREX, from the beginning or more recently. We've built a community with its own identity, friendships, rivalries and memorable moments. I'm not a perfect owner, teammate or player, so when I talk about standards, I'm including myself.

**What I want isn't perfection.** Nobody has to play flawlessly, agree on everything or give every free hour. What I do want is consistency in how we represent NOREX: playing as a team, respecting each other's time, communicating, taking fair criticism, and making small sacrifices for the squad. Sometimes that means a new position, giving someone else a chance, or accepting a manager's decision.

**Rules aren't there to take the fun out.** They exist to avoid misunderstandings and repeat arguments so we spend more time enjoying football together.

**Community and competition were never opposites.** We once sat among the top clubs, second or third, without chasing it. Along the way, protecting the community, we drifted from that competitive side. I don't regret putting people first, but we never had to give up one for the other. No ranking is worth losing the people who made this club.

These standards apply to everyone, management and longtime members included. Mistakes, jokes, respectful disagreement and off days are all fine.

Nobody is obligated to be part of NOREX. If this direction suits you, I hope you stay. If it doesn't, no hard feelings.

## What happens next
Everyone has **one week** to read the updated club documents and accept them on the web app. This isn't an ultimatum. If someone chooses not to accept, I'll respect that, and if most of the club prefers to carry on as it is, I'll respect that too.

**We don't need perfect players. We need people willing to be good teammates.**

NOREX UNITED F.C.

items.title: Our club philosophy
items.body:
NOREX UNITED was built around a community worth being part of and a team that takes pride in competing. We want to find that balance again and build beyond it without losing the people who made it possible.

## The club comes first
No player, manager, founder or individual record is above the club. Skill matters, but so do respect, reliability, awareness and making the players around you better.

## Competition without pressure to be perfect
We want to win and improve: good decisions, playing our roles, supporting teammates, learning from hard matches. That doesn't mean flawless performances, endless availability, or trading friendships for a leaderboard spot.

## Fair chances and shared responsibility
A place in a competitive lineup is earned through contribution, teamwork, availability and what the squad needs, never favoritism. Players get clear communication and real chances to develop. In return, everyone adapts, accepts feedback and sometimes puts the squad ahead of their first preference.

## How we move forward
We're not replacing the club we built. We're restoring the link between community and competitive football that once defined us: a NOREX where people enjoy showing up, trust their teammates and take pride in how we play.

items.title: 1. Respect every member
items.body: Treat teammates, opponents and staff with respect. No personal attacks, discrimination, harassment, threats or targeted humiliation. Banter is fine while it is mutual; stop when someone says it is unwelcome.

items.title: 2. Play for the team
items.body: Rush and League are team modes. Use your teammates, spot passing options, make supporting runs and help defend. Creativity is welcome; repeatedly ignoring the team to force personal plays is not.

items.title: 3. Respect your position and the setup
items.body: Play the role you accepted and keep the team shape. Don't abandon your assignment or change the approach mid-match without saying so. Discuss positional changes between games or when the squad agrees.

items.title: 4. Do not disrupt matches
items.body: No intentional own goals, sabotage, trolling teammates or quitting just to punish the squad. If you have to leave, tell the group when you can.

items.title: 5. Keep match communication constructive
items.body: Call out runs, mark assignments, give useful feedback. Avoid constant blame, shouting over others and long arguments mid-play. Save detailed disagreements for after the match.

items.title: 6. Be fair with lobby spots and rotations
items.body: Nobody owns a lobby or is entitled to every match. When demand beats spots, staff communicate the selection or rotation plan. Competitive lineups may favor fit and readiness, but never personally.

items.title: 7. Respect the North American playing region
items.body: NOREX organizes sessions around North American connections to keep play fair and playable. Follow the region and connection requirements for organized sessions and don't knowingly bypass an eligibility decision.

items.title: 8. Honor match-night commitments
items.body: If you confirm a match or tournament, arrive ready and tell the organizer promptly if that changes. Repeated no-shows without notice may affect future selection.

items.title: 9. Follow competition-specific rules
items.body: Tournament roster limits, club eligibility, suspensions, scheduling and match reporting follow the rules published for that event. Casual lobby habits don't carry over.

items.title: 10. Respect decisions, keep the right to question them
items.body: You can challenge a decision respectfully. Raise concerns privately with the manager or founder, not as a public confrontation. Staff must listen and explain when appropriate.

items.title: 11. No favoritism or misuse of staff roles
items.body: Managers and the founder follow the same conduct rules as everyone. Staff must not use access, roles or lineup authority to settle personal disagreements.

items.title: 12. Protect the community
items.body: Don't share private member information, impersonate others or use NOREX channels to target members. Respect Discord channel purposes and official communications.

items.title: 13. Accept feedback and take responsibility
items.body: Mistakes happen. Own them, listen to reasonable feedback and give others the same chance to improve. Repeatedly refusing to cooperate is different from an off game.

items.title: 14. How rule issues are handled
items.body: Staff weigh context, impact and repeated behavior. Responses range from a conversation or warning to temporary exclusion from organized sessions, removal of a staff role, or removal from the club. Serious misconduct may warrant immediate action. You can ask the founder to review any decision.

items.title: What members can expect, and what we ask
items.body:
## You can expect
Respectful treatment, clear rules, honest communication, chances to play and develop, and a fair process when concerns come up. Nobody can promise a starting spot or preferred position every session.

## We ask
Be reliable when you commit, respect the squad, make an honest effort in your assigned role and be willing to adapt. You don't have to be the best player in the lobby, but you do need to add to the experience of those playing with you.

items.title: What managers are responsible for
items.body:
- Organize sessions and communicate lineup and rotation decisions.
- Welcome and assess trial players fairly.
- Explain the approach for organized matches.
- Handle issues without favoritism, lead by example and take reasonable criticism.

## Playing time and selection
Casual sessions should make room for fair rotation. Competitive matches may need a set lineup, formation or role balance. Managers stay transparent about which is which and never treat friendship as a selection criterion.

## Resolving disagreements
Talk directly and respectfully, ideally after a match. If it continues, contact a manager or the founder with the details. Everyone involved gets a fair chance to explain before a decision is made.

## Recognition
Awards look beyond goals and assists: defending, chance creation, positioning, smart passing, clutch moments, reliability, improvement and helping teammates.

items.title: How we play: Rush, League and Grounds
items.body:
## Rush: five players, shared responsibility
Keep passing lanes open, give the ball carrier options and rotate sensibly when teammates push up. Defending belongs to everyone; don't leave one player isolated at the back or force skills when a team option is clear. Quick decisions and chemistry beat individual highlights.

## League: structure and coordination
Respect the chosen formation and positions. Keep width and balance, call runs and defensive cover, and work through midfield instead of forcing every attack. Selection weighs availability, role fit, coordination and team needs.

## Grounds: room to experiment
Test builds, movement, camera settings and ideas with teammates who know the session's purpose. Agree when a lobby is experimental. Testing never excuses wasting teammates' time.

## Before a session
Confirm the mode, positions, whether the lobby is competitive or experimental, and how extra players rotate. If you're leaving early or testing a build, say so first.

## After a difficult match
Keep feedback specific: a passing option, missing cover, a formation tweak. No personal attacks. Agree what to change and move into the next game together.

items.title: Welcome to NOREX UNITED
items.body:
NOREX is a North American EA FC27 club built around competitive football and a strong community. Read our philosophy and rules, connect on Discord and check the available Rush, League and Grounds sessions.

## Before joining a lobby
Check the mode and open positions. Tell the squad if you're testing a build or only available briefly. If the lobby is full, ask about rotation or another session instead of interrupting a match.

## Organized match reminder
If you confirm attendance, check the posted schedule and lineup, arrive ready, and tell the organizer as soon as you know you can't make it.

items.title: Do I need to be an elite player?
items.body: No. We value effort, awareness, cooperation and improvement. Organized competitive lineups may need particular roles or readiness, but everyone gets respectful treatment and a fair opportunity.

items.title: Can I play any position?
items.body: You can ask to try a new one. For an organized match, agree the change with the manager or squad first.

items.title: Are skill moves or solo goals discouraged?
items.body: No, creativity is part of football. The concern is repeatedly ignoring teammates or forcing plays that hurt the squad.

items.title: What if I disagree with a decision?
items.body: Raise it respectfully with the manager after the match, or take it to the founder if it stays unresolved. Disagreement is allowed; personal attacks and public pile-ons are not.

items.title: Why does connection region matter?
items.body: We focus on North American play to reduce unfair lag and keep matches consistent for the squad.

items.title: Where do I find official updates?
items.body: On the NOREX website and in the Discord announcement areas. A rumor or casual message is not an official rule change.

items.title: Where do I confirm the updated rules and vision?
items.body: Use the acceptance option on the NOREX web app during the one-week review period announced by the founder.

items.title: Match-night conduct
items.body: Be on time, be kind, play for the badge. No quitting mid-match.

items.title: Rotation rules
items.body: Everyone plays. Starters follow availability and form.

Not an official EA source - unverified until confirmed in-game or in EA Pitch Notes. Never edit a published file: publish a new version instead.

sources.title: Pitch Notes – The Grounds & Clubs Deep Dive

levelCap.note: Matches the community-reported cap already on record (unverified). Community dataset tag: 2026-09-28.

rules.text: Every archetype is unlocked from the start; progression (AXP) is per archetype.
Archetype resets no longer cost coins or a reset consumable.
Levelling an archetype unlocks Masteries – small permanent attribute boosts for every archetype (e.g. Finisher level 10: +1 Finishing, +1 Composure).
Amps are temporary boosts for the active archetype (tiers 1–4, higher tiers add PlayStyles/PlayStyles+ and perks). At launch, Amps give no PlayStyle+.
AXP consumables can have their own level caps, always within the global max level.

playstyles.name: Finesse Shot
playstyles.desc: Performs Finesse Shots faster with additional curve and improved accuracy.

playstyles.name: Chip Shot
playstyles.desc: Performs Chip Shots faster and with greater accuracy.

playstyles.name: Power Shot
playstyles.desc: Performs Power Shots faster and with increased speed.

playstyles.name: Dead Ball
playstyles.desc: Set pieces are delivered with increased speed, curve, and accuracy. Ball trajectory preview line is longer.

playstyles.name: Precision Header
playstyles.desc: Performs headers with increased accuracy and has access to Precision Header animations.

playstyles.name: Acrobatic
playstyles.desc: Performs volleys with improved accuracy and has access to acrobatic volley animations.

playstyles.name: Low Driven Shot
playstyles.desc: Enhances a player's ability to execute low driven shots with increased accuracy, faster ball travel, and quicker shot execution.

playstyles.name: Gamechanger
playstyles.desc: Enables a player to perform Trivela shots. Fancy shots are performed with higher accuracy. Performs Gamechanger animations when contextually appropriate.

playstyles.name: Incisive Pass
playstyles.desc: Through Passes are more accurate, swerve passes are delivered with more curve, and Precision Passes travel faster to the destination.

playstyles.name: Pinged Pass
playstyles.desc: Passes travel faster along the ground without impacting the trapping difficulty of the receiver.

playstyles.name: Long Ball Pass
playstyles.desc: Lob and Lofted Through Passes are more accurate, travel faster and are more difficult to intercept.

playstyles.name: Tiki Taka
playstyles.desc: Executes difficult first-time Ground Passes with high accuracy, using backheels when contextually appropriate. Short distance Ground Passes are highly accurate.

playstyles.name: Whipped Pass
playstyles.desc: All crosses are highly accurate, travel faster and with more curve.

playstyles.name: Inventive
playstyles.desc: Fancy passes, including outside-of-the-foot passes, are performed with improved accuracy. Performs Inventive animations when contextually appropriate.

playstyles.name: Jockey
playstyles.desc: Increased max speed of Sprint Jockey and improved transition speed from jockey to sprint.

playstyles.name: Block
playstyles.desc: Increased reach when performing blocks and improved ability to make a successful block.

playstyles.name: Intercept
playstyles.desc: Increased reach and improved chances of retaining possession of the ball when performing interceptions.

playstyles.name: Anticipate
playstyles.desc: Improved chances of standing tackle success and grants the ability to stop the ball directly at their feet when performing a standing tackle.

playstyles.name: Slide Tackle
playstyles.desc: Grants the ability to stop the ball directly at their feet when performing a slide tackle.

playstyles.name: Aerial Fortress
playstyles.desc: Performs higher jumps and has improved defensive aerial presence.

playstyles.name: Technical
playstyles.desc: Reaches a higher speed when performing Controlled Sprint and performs wide turns while dribbling with more precision.

playstyles.name: Rapid
playstyles.desc: Reaches a higher sprint speed while dribbling and has reduced chance of an error when sprinting or performing knock-ons.

playstyles.name: First Touch
playstyles.desc: Has reduced error when trapping the ball and is able to transition to dribbling faster with greater control.

playstyles.name: Trickster
playstyles.desc: Grants the ability to perform unique ground and flick Skill Moves.

playstyles.name: Press Proven
playstyles.desc: Keeps close control of the ball while dribbling at jog speed and can shield the ball more effectively from stronger opponents.

playstyles.name: Quick Step
playstyles.desc: Accelerates faster during Explosive Sprint.

playstyles.name: Relentless
playstyles.desc: Increases stamina regeneration speed. Increases the duration of teammate contain and partial team press.

playstyles.name: Long Throw
playstyles.desc: Performs throw-ins with increased power to cover a greater distance.

playstyles.name: Bruiser
playstyles.desc: Greater strength when performing physical tackles.

playstyles.name: Enforcer
playstyles.desc: Greater strength when performing shield dribbles.

playstyles.name: Far Throw
playstyles.desc: Unique GK throw animations and increased GK throw max distance.

playstyles.name: Footwork
playstyles.desc: Exclusive foot save animations and increased performance against low trajectory shots.

playstyles.name: Cross Claimer
playstyles.desc: Unique punching animations, increased hand strength and ball out speed from punches, prioritization of punch animations in contested ball scenarios, and increased speed for coming out for crosses.

playstyles.name: 1v1 Close Down
playstyles.desc: Unique reflex/anticipation save animations, increase in rush speed and improved read of close shot trajectories.

playstyles.name: Far Reach
playstyles.desc: Unique long diving distance jump animations and increased chances of saving long distance shots.

playstyles.name: Deflector
playstyles.desc: Unique animations for push deflect, dive push deflect, and regular deflects. Increases the ball out speed from deflections and improves the probability of deflecting to safer areas.

items.title: A message from the founder
items.body:
To everyone representing NOREX UNITED,

I appreciate everyone who has been part of NOREX, from the beginning or more recently. We've built a community with its own identity, friendships, rivalries and memorable moments. I'm not a perfect owner, teammate or player, so when I talk about standards, I'm including myself.

**What I want isn't perfection.** Nobody has to play flawlessly, agree on everything or give every free hour. What I do want is consistency in how we represent NOREX: playing as a team, respecting each other's time, communicating, taking fair criticism, and making small sacrifices for the squad. Sometimes that means a new position, giving someone else a chance, or accepting a manager's decision.

**Rules aren't there to take the fun out.** They exist to avoid misunderstandings and repeat arguments so we spend more time enjoying football together.

**Community and competition were never opposites.** We once sat among the top clubs, second or third, without chasing it. Along the way, protecting the community, we drifted from that competitive side. I don't regret putting people first, but we never had to give up one for the other. No ranking is worth losing the people who made this club.

These standards apply to everyone, management and longtime members included. Mistakes, jokes, respectful disagreement and off days are all fine.

Nobody is obligated to be part of NOREX. If this direction suits you, I hope you stay. If it doesn't, no hard feelings.

## What happens next
Everyone has **one week** to read the updated club documents and accept them on the web app. This isn't an ultimatum. If someone chooses not to accept, I'll respect that, and if most of the club prefers to carry on as it is, I'll respect that too.

**We don't need perfect players. We need people willing to be good teammates.**

NOREX UNITED F.C.

items.title: Our club philosophy
items.body:
NOREX UNITED was built around a community worth being part of and a team that takes pride in competing. We want to find that balance again and build beyond it without losing the people who made it possible.

## The club comes first
No player, manager, founder or individual record is above the club. Skill matters, but so do respect, reliability, awareness and making the players around you better.

## Competition without pressure to be perfect
We want to win and improve: good decisions, playing our roles, supporting teammates, learning from hard matches. That doesn't mean flawless performances, endless availability, or trading friendships for a leaderboard spot.

## Fair chances and shared responsibility
A place in a competitive lineup is earned through contribution, teamwork, availability and what the squad needs, never favoritism. Players get clear communication and real chances to develop. In return, everyone adapts, accepts feedback and sometimes puts the squad ahead of their first preference.

## How we move forward
We're not replacing the club we built. We're restoring the link between community and competitive football that once defined us: a NOREX where people enjoy showing up, trust their teammates and take pride in how we play.

items.title: 1. Respect every member
items.body: Treat teammates, opponents and staff with respect. No personal attacks, discrimination, harassment, threats or targeted humiliation. Banter is fine while it is mutual; stop when someone says it is unwelcome.

items.title: 2. Play for the team
items.body: Rush and League are team modes. Use your teammates, spot passing options, make supporting runs and help defend. Creativity is welcome; repeatedly ignoring the team to force personal plays is not.

items.title: 3. Respect your position and the setup
items.body: Play the role you accepted and keep the team shape. Don't abandon your assignment or change the approach mid-match without saying so. Discuss positional changes between games or when the squad agrees.

items.title: 4. Do not disrupt matches
items.body: No intentional own goals, sabotage, trolling teammates or quitting just to punish the squad. If you have to leave, tell the group when you can.

items.title: 5. Keep match communication constructive
items.body: Call out runs, mark assignments, give useful feedback. Avoid constant blame, shouting over others and long arguments mid-play. Save detailed disagreements for after the match.

items.title: 6. Be fair with lobby spots and rotations
items.body: Nobody owns a lobby or is entitled to every match. When demand beats spots, staff communicate the selection or rotation plan. Competitive lineups may favor fit and readiness, but never personally.

items.title: 7. Respect the North American playing region
items.body: NOREX organizes sessions around North American connections to keep play fair and playable. Follow the region and connection requirements for organized sessions and don't knowingly bypass an eligibility decision.

items.title: 8. Honor match-night commitments
items.body: If you confirm a match or tournament, arrive ready and tell the organizer promptly if that changes. Repeated no-shows without notice may affect future selection.

items.title: 9. Follow competition-specific rules
items.body: Tournament roster limits, club eligibility, suspensions, scheduling and match reporting follow the rules published for that event. Casual lobby habits don't carry over.

items.title: 10. Respect decisions, keep the right to question them
items.body: You can challenge a decision respectfully. Raise concerns privately with the manager or founder, not as a public confrontation. Staff must listen and explain when appropriate.

items.title: 11. No favoritism or misuse of staff roles
items.body: Managers and the founder follow the same conduct rules as everyone. Staff must not use access, roles or lineup authority to settle personal disagreements.

items.title: 12. Protect the community
items.body: Don't share private member information, impersonate others or use NOREX channels to target members. Respect Discord channel purposes and official communications.

items.title: 13. Accept feedback and take responsibility
items.body: Mistakes happen. Own them, listen to reasonable feedback and give others the same chance to improve. Repeatedly refusing to cooperate is different from an off game.

items.title: 14. How rule issues are handled
items.body: Staff weigh context, impact and repeated behavior. Responses range from a conversation or warning to temporary exclusion from organized sessions, removal of a staff role, or removal from the club. Serious misconduct may warrant immediate action. You can ask the founder to review any decision.

items.title: What members can expect, and what we ask
items.body:
## You can expect
Respectful treatment, clear rules, honest communication, chances to play and develop, and a fair process when concerns come up. Nobody can promise a starting spot or preferred position every session.

## We ask
Be reliable when you commit, respect the squad, make an honest effort in your assigned role and be willing to adapt. You don't have to be the best player in the lobby, but you do need to add to the experience of those playing with you.

items.title: What managers are responsible for
items.body:
- Organize sessions and communicate lineup and rotation decisions.
- Welcome and assess trial players fairly.
- Explain the approach for organized matches.
- Handle issues without favoritism, lead by example and take reasonable criticism.

## Playing time and selection
Casual sessions should make room for fair rotation. Competitive matches may need a set lineup, formation or role balance. Managers stay transparent about which is which and never treat friendship as a selection criterion.

## Resolving disagreements
Talk directly and respectfully, ideally after a match. If it continues, contact a manager or the founder with the details. Everyone involved gets a fair chance to explain before a decision is made.

## Recognition
Awards look beyond goals and assists: defending, chance creation, positioning, smart passing, clutch moments, reliability, improvement and helping teammates.

items.title: How we play: Rush, League and Grounds
items.body:
## Rush: five players, shared responsibility
Keep passing lanes open, give the ball carrier options and rotate sensibly when teammates push up. Defending belongs to everyone; don't leave one player isolated at the back or force skills when a team option is clear. Quick decisions and chemistry beat individual highlights.

## League: structure and coordination
Respect the chosen formation and positions. Keep width and balance, call runs and defensive cover, and work through midfield instead of forcing every attack. Selection weighs availability, role fit, coordination and team needs.

## Grounds: room to experiment
Test builds, movement, camera settings and ideas with teammates who know the session's purpose. Agree when a lobby is experimental. Testing never excuses wasting teammates' time.

## Before a session
Confirm the mode, positions, whether the lobby is competitive or experimental, and how extra players rotate. If you're leaving early or testing a build, say so first.

## After a difficult match
Keep feedback specific: a passing option, missing cover, a formation tweak. No personal attacks. Agree what to change and move into the next game together.

items.title: Welcome to NOREX UNITED
items.body:
NOREX is a North American EA FC27 club built around competitive football and a strong community. Read our philosophy and rules, connect on Discord and check the available Rush, League and Grounds sessions.

## Before joining a lobby
Check the mode and open positions. Tell the squad if you're testing a build or only available briefly. If the lobby is full, ask about rotation or another session instead of interrupting a match.

## Organized match reminder
If you confirm attendance, check the posted schedule and lineup, arrive ready, and tell the organizer as soon as you know you can't make it.

items.title: Do I need to be an elite player?
items.body: No. We value effort, awareness, cooperation and improvement. Organized competitive lineups may need particular roles or readiness, but everyone gets respectful treatment and a fair opportunity.

items.title: Can I play any position?
items.body: You can ask to try a new one. For an organized match, agree the change with the manager or squad first.

items.title: Are skill moves or solo goals discouraged?
items.body: No, creativity is part of football. The concern is repeatedly ignoring teammates or forcing plays that hurt the squad.

items.title: What if I disagree with a decision?
items.body: Raise it respectfully with the manager after the match, or take it to the founder if it stays unresolved. Disagreement is allowed; personal attacks and public pile-ons are not.

items.title: Why does connection region matter?
items.body: We focus on North American play to reduce unfair lag and keep matches consistent for the squad.

items.title: Where do I find official updates?
items.body: On the NOREX website and in the Discord announcement areas. A rumor or casual message is not an official rule change.

items.title: Where do I confirm the updated rules and vision?
items.body: Use the acceptance option on the NOREX web app during the one-week review period announced by the founder.

items.title: Match-night conduct
items.body: Be on time, be kind, play for the badge. No quitting mid-match.

items.title: Rotation rules
items.body: Everyone plays. Starters follow availability and form.

items.body: Apply with your EA ID and a position. A manager will invite you to a trial night.

items.body: Managers pick from availability, form and position needs.
